text: Twenty-six minutes sounds like nothing. It's a whole year.
A full year of your life, nonstop, no sleep. Sounds fake— okay, let's prove it.
Back in twenty twenty-two, the average commute in America was about twenty-six minutes each way, says the Census.
Round trip, that's almost an hour a day. Annoying, but fine, right?
Smash like if your commute laughs at twenty-six minutes.
Now times two hundred fifty workdays a year.
That's two hundred twenty hours a year. That's like nine days straight in your car.
Then do that for forty years of work.
Send this to the friend who swears their commute is short.
Eight thousand eight hundred hours. Wait, what does that even mean?
Divide by twenty-four. It's three hundred sixty-seven days. A full calendar year, around the clock.
Here's the twist. Say your time is worth the middle wage, about twenty-four fifty-one an hour.
Then that commute is worth around two hundred fifteen thousand dollars.
Follow if you want more math that ruins your morning drive.
And your paycheck covers exactly zero of it.
Love the drive or hate it, it's still a whole year of your life.
So how many minutes is yours, one way? Be honest.
